paragraphs.text: Qing-so-Yui, Minceu or Xiao Hai-ki.
Hai-ki, Chapter 1.
A Mountain Home.
It was a hot morning in June in the Alps.
Hai-ki walked behind her aunt named Ete.
They were walking through the village and up the mountain.
Hai-ki was very hot because she was wearing all her clothes.
She had to carry them to her new home.
She was only six years old.
As Hai-ki and her aunt hurried out of the village,
a villager stopped to talk.
Dae-te, is this the orphan your sister left when she died?
Where are you taking her?
Yes, this is Hai-te.
I'm taking her to live with her grandfather.
I'm starting a job in the city, so I can't take care of her anymore.
Poor Hai-te, said the villager.
No one else will talk to that grumpy old man.
While Dae-te was talking with the villager, Hai-te met a boy named Peter.
He was the village goat herder.
Every morning, Peter came to the village to get the goats.
He was going to take them up the mountain.
Hai-te followed him up the mountain.
She couldn't keep up with him because of her heavy clothes.
So she took off all of them except her underwear.
Then she danced behind Peter.
He thought she was funny.
The two children began laughing.
Dae-te caught up with them.
Where are your clothes?
She asked.
I don't need them.
Hai-te said.
I want to run free like the goats.
And Dae-te scolded Hai-te and sent Peter to get her clothes.
They walked for another hour.
Near the mountaintop was Grandfather's hut.
The old man was sitting in front of the house.
Hai-te ran up to him and held out her hand.
Hello, Grandfather.
She said he held her hand and stared at her.
Good morning, Uncle.
Said Dae-te.
Hai-te must stay with you now.
She explained why she couldn't take care of the child anymore.
The old man was angry.
You can just get out of here.
He yelled at Dae-te.
Aunt Dae-te said goodbye to Hai-te very quickly and left.
Hai-te looked around her new home.
Where can I sleep?
Asked Hai-te.
Anywhere you want.
Answered Grandfather.
Hai-te saw a ladder behind the bed.
She climbed the ladder up to the loft.
The loft was filled with fresh hay.
I'll sleep up here.
Said Hai-te happily.
Hai-te followed Grandfather everywhere.
She watched as he made a new chair for her.
When the sun was setting, Hai-te heard a whistle.
It was Peter bringing the goats home.
Grandfather had two goats.
Their names were Daisy and Dusky.
Hai-te liked them at once.
The next morning, Peter's whistle woke Hai-te.
She got ready to go with Peter.
She was excited.
The mountain was very beautiful.
Hai-te picked flowers and chased the goats.
Peter told her all of the goats' names.
Hai-te was sad when she heard that a little goat had lost its mother.
She promised to take special care of that goat.
By now the sun was setting.
It spread a golden glow across the tops of the mountains.
Peter?
cried Hai-te.
The mountains are on fire.
Don't worry.
replied Peter.
That happens every day.
It means it's time to go home.
Hai-te went up the mountain with Peter every day during the summer.
She grew to be healthy and strong.
She was as free as a bird.
But when the phone came, Grandfather made her stay at home.
He was afraid the strong winds would blow her off the mountain.
She spent the days helping him make cheese.
Then came the winter and lots of snow.
Peter went to school in the winter.
One day he came to the hunt.
He told Hai-te that his grandmother would like to meet her.
She wanted to go, but Grandfather said the snow was too deep.
A few days later the snow finally stopped.
The sun came out and Grandfather said she could go out.
He put Hai-te on his sled.
The sled raced down the mountain very fast.
Grandfather stopped the sled in front of Peter's small hut.
Hai-te met an old woman that was sewing.
Hello, Granny.
Said Hai-te.
Granny smiled and felt Hai-te's hand.
Granny was blind.
Why can't you see?
asked Hai-te.
I can't see.
Granny said kindly, but I can hear.
Hai-te spent the rest of the winter with Granny.
Sometimes Grandfather came and fixed the windows and chairs in Granny's hut.
